ap.conversion: Bartels' standard Kp-to-ap conversion table (GFZ Potsdam); 28 values, one per third of a Kp unit, looked up rather than fitted.
ap.derivedFrom: the planetary Kp series published in this release

f107.quantity: 10.7 cm solar radio flux, daily noon value

f107a.basis: NOAA's published 90-day running mean of the same 10.7 cm flux. NRLMSIS defines F10.7A as the 81-day mean centred on the day, which cannot be computed for today because it needs forty days of the future.

thermosphereEmpirical.limitation: Systematically under-responds to geomagnetic storms. See CURATED_DENSITY_EVENTS for the size of the discrepancy against published measurements.
thermosphereEmpirical.product: NRLMSIS 2.1, evaluated from NOAA SWPC F10.7 and Kp-derived ap
thermosphereEmpirical.representation: The US Naval Research Laboratory's empirical model, a published fit to decades of observations, evaluated from F10.7 and Ap alone. Not a measurement and not a physics simulation: a statistical description of how the atmosphere usually behaves.

publishedControls.blockingReason: The payload flag rate is only 6.9 times the false-alarm floor once both are read at their 95 per cent bounds, against the 10 times this site requires before an individual event may be called a manoeuvre. Up to one flag in 7 on a payload could be the same noise.
publishedControls.matchedControlStatus: not enabled: matched-control acceptance has not been measured
publishedControls.note: Debris and spent rocket stages have no propulsion, so every flag on one is a false alarm by construction. The interval is Jeffreys rather than Wald: at zero flags Wald would report a false-alarm rate of exactly zero, which no control can support.

rateSeparation.gap: The payload flag rate is only 6.9 times the false-alarm floor once both are read at their 95 per cent bounds, against the 10 times this site requires before an individual event may be called a manoeuvre. Up to one flag in 7 on a payload could be the same noise.
rateSeparation.note: Lower bound on the payload rate against upper bound on the passive rate. Bounds rather than point estimates, and an effect size rather than a p-value: with tens of millions of intervals a two-proportion test is significant for a ratio of 1.001, which would say the archive is large rather than that the detector separates the two populations.

separation.caution: The normal approximation is poor when either count is below about ten. Treat this as an order-of-magnitude statement about significance, not a precise p-value.

strataDefinition.edges: upper edges inclusive, exactly as CATALOGUE_NOISE_FLOOR: 500, 800, 1500, 30000 km

publishedCoverage.framing: These are fitted mean elements published every few hours, not measurements of where a satellite is. What this archive can show you is how the fit moved.

noDataIntervals.note: Nothing before this point is held. What the archive does hold is whatever the hourly capture has seen since it started, plus whatever the bulk back-fill has imported from space-track's published yearly bundles.

The archive holds element sets on both sides of this gap and none inside it: the bulk bundles end before live capture began. Nothing is interpolated across it, no cadence is measured across it, and an operator-published manoeuvre inside it is recorded as unscorable rather than as one the detector missed.
